add.issue.name: Settings panel: the gear does not close a panel the avatar opened; Escape in a dropdown closes the panel; an armed trash never disarms

edit.description.md:
Review of 4SC2RXY at 858da367 (`SettingsPanel.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `ReposSettings.tsx`). Each reproduced in the browser. All small; fine after merge.

**1. The gear does not close.** `toggleSettings` in App.tsx closes only when the panel is open at the gear's own focus (`overview`), so a panel opened from the avatar or the palette's Link repo stays open on the first gear click, while the gear is drawn pressed. Fix: the gear closes whenever the panel is open.

**2. Escape in a dropdown closes the panel.** The Dropdown's Menu and the panel both use `useDismissOnOutsideClick`, which listens on the document; one Escape fires both, so picking branches and backing out loses the panel. The URL field already stops propagation; the Menu should too, or the hook should honour `defaultPrevented`.

**3. The trash stays armed.** `useArmed` in ReposSettings has no blur or outside-click disarm (the claim button has `onBlur`), so a row stays washed red until another trash is pressed or the panel closes.

Nits: `fetchLinkedRepos` (e2e-gui/linked-repos.ts) sets `process.env.EPIQ_GLOBAL_DIR` for the rest of the worker; `IdentityPanel.tsx` now exports `IdentityAddresses`.

add.issue.name: Other repos: a linked repo with no commits yet reads as "its history could not be read" under the default branch

edit.description.md:
Full-feature review of 4SC2RXY at 858da367, `source/lib/commits/commit-sources.ts:97`. Reproduced through the real code (fetch, then `listRepoStates`).

A clone under `branches: default` is read with `git log HEAD`. On a remote with no commits yet HEAD is an unborn branch, and git answers `fatal: your current branch 'main' does not have any commits yet` (exit 128). The fetch itself reports ok and the timeline reads as empty, but `readSourceLogs` notes the failure, so the panel's row shows "its history could not be read" and an info line is logged per fetch. Under `branches: all` the read is `--branches`, which answers nothing and succeeds.

Fix: `--branches` for both settings (a default clone holds only the default branch: the refspec fetches one, and `dropOtherBranches` removes the rest after a switch), or `--branches=<name>` from the clone's HEAD. Add the empty-remote case to the reading tests.

Fine after merge.

add.issue.name: Settings panel: never takes focus nor hands it back; a label rename makes every client refetch its history

edit.description.md:
Full-feature review of 4SC2RXY at 858da367, GUI surface.

**1. Focus (after merge, an a11y regression).** `SettingsPanel.tsx:264`, the `role="dialog"` root, never takes focus on open and never returns it on close. Opened from the keyboard (gear focused, Enter) focus stays on the gear; Tab lands on the avatar outside the dialog; after Escape focus is wherever it drifted. The repos modal this replaced took focus once on mount and handed it back (DASQEJQ). Only the URL field has `autoFocus`, and only after "link a repo". Reproduced with Playwright reading `document.activeElement`. Also: neither the gear (`aria-pressed`) nor the avatar (`aria-label`) carries `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` for the dialog.

**2. A rename refetches everything (nit).** `websocket.ts:512-514` broadcasts `repos:changed` unless the answer is `Unchanged`; a label-only change answers `Renamed …`, so every client re-asks the list, the timeline window and the open ticket's commits for a change that moved no commit. The server keeps its clone-log cache for a rename; the clients do not. Reproduced: Enter on the label field sent `repo:add`, `repos:get`, `timeline:get`, `commits:get`.

**Nits.** `SettingsPanel.tsx:161-170` measures `top` on mount and resize only, so a FollowBanner appearing or leaving while the panel is open leaves a gap or an overlap until a resize. Every socket connect sends `repos:get`, and each one spawns `git config --get remote.origin.url` via `readOwnRepo`, even on a board with no repos and the panel never opened. A repo unticked in a wide window and absent from a narrower one has no toggle there and is shown, then hidden again on widening: by design, but it reads as the chart forgetting.

add.issue.name: Other repos: another worktree's sweep clears a remove tombstone before the waiting pass reaches it; two new tests do not bite

edit.description.md:
Re-review of 4SC2RXY at 85d16db2. All after merge.

**1. Tombstone swept too early (reproduced).** `sweepPending` (`commit-repo-fetch.ts`) removes a `<id>.git.removed` tombstone once no clone stands under it and the sweeping pass's own list lacks the repo. A pass in another worktree of the same project starts, sweeps it, and the pass in this worktree that read its list before the remove, and was waiting on the clone's lock or its batch, then finds no mark and clones the removed repo again, answering `Fetched`. The orphan clone names no listed repo and `repo remove` cannot reach it. Probe: hold R's clone lock, start a pass on board A, release, unregister R, start a pass on board B (same projectId, lists only another repo), await A: clone exists, R unlisted. Without B's pass it stays removed ("Removed before it was cloned"). Fix: don't sweep tombstones; clear one on re-add (upsert) and in `deleteClone`, as now. They are empty files.

**2. The empty-remote test reads state before the read.** `commit-repos-hostile.test.ts` "a remote with no commits yet" calls `listRepoStates` before `getCommitsForRef`; the "could not be read" note is only set by a timeline read, so it stays green with `HEAD` restored in `commit-sources.ts`. Read commits first, then the state. (Red with the read first: probe run.)

**3. "a remove that lands while a pass is waiting" exercises the mark, not the tombstone.** It calls `removeRepoClone` while the test still holds the lock, so the remove takes the mark path; the new `removalMark` write after `deleteClone` can be deleted and the test stays green. Release the lock before the remove. (Red that way: probe run.)

The fixes themselves are right: both probes go red with the fix reverted and green with it.

add.issue.comment.md:
Review of the disk cap in ea73ae87 (`H9SEJN2-repo-hardening`), pinned; the branch untouched. Gate green: lint, both typechecks, prettier, unit 2329, GUI e2e 229.

The undo is sound against what was asked:
- Git stopped mid-pack, reproduced through the real fetch over a throttled ssh wrapper (8 MB under a 2 MB cap, cut off after 4.3s of ~13s). The tip is the old one, the pack dir holds only the old pack, there are no temp packs or lock files, no git or index-pack survives, and `fsck --full` is clean. With the cap raised, the next fetch lands whole and reads both commits.
- `.keep`, `.rev` and every other new pack-dir file go with the pack. Temp packs and `incoming-` dirs are cleared only after git has exited. FETCH_HEAD stays stale, which nothing reads.
- The restore and the lock tests both fail with their fix reverted.

`fetch.unpackLimit=1`: no effect on clone, which always keeps a pack. Deepen and unshallow are fetches and keep theirs.

After merge:
- Commit-graph and reflogs are not in the snapshot. With `fetch.writeCommitGraph=true` in the user's config, a capped fetch leaves a commit-graph naming the deleted commits. Reproduced at the git level: on git 2.39 the next fetch downloads them again and `fsck --full` is clean, so it is harmless here. Pinning `fetch.writeCommitGraph=false` and `core.logAllRefUpdates=false` in cloneGitConfig removes the case outright.
- Pack growth: with `unpackLimit=1` and `gc.auto=0`, every fetch that brings commits adds a pack that nothing consolidates. Object lookups and `dirSize` both slow as the count grows. A `repack -d` under the clone lock past some pack count would bound it, counting its temporary doubling against the cap.
- `dirSize` is a synchronous walk whose cost is file count, not bytes: 44 ms over the 15,120 files of epiq's own `.git`, run once a second during a transfer on the GUI server's event loop. Cheap for a packed clone. Walking only `objects/` asynchronously would bound it.
- Windows, by reading: without a process group the abort kills git but not its index-pack. The 6s fallback answer can then restore while the helper still writes, and a pack lands after the undo.

Nothing I would hold the merge for.

add.issue.name: Linked repos: a default switch whose fetch hits the cap leaves the old default branch read for good

edit.description.md:
Post-merge review of main at 903a8ade, `commit-repo-fetch.ts` `fetchRepo`. Reproduced through the real fetch.

`fetchRepo` follows a switched remote default before the transfer: `followDefaultBranch` repoints HEAD and `remote.origin.fetch`. If the cap then stops the transfer, the undo restores refs, packed-refs and shallow, but not HEAD or the config. The next successful fetch sees HEAD already on the new default, so it neither follows (`followed` stays false) nor runs `dropOtherBranches`. The old default's ref is never dropped, and under `branches: default` the clone reads two branches.

Probe: upstream on `main`, cloned under a 2 MB cap. The upstream's HEAD moves to `trunk`, which gains a 6 MB blob. The fetch is capped and afterwards holds heads `main`, HEAD `refs/heads/trunk`. With the cap raised, the next fetch leaves heads `main` and `trunk`, and the ticket's commits include `AAAAAAA main only`, which is on the old default only.

Fix, either way: add HEAD and `remote.origin.fetch` to the snapshot the undo restores, or under `default` run `dropOtherBranches` on every successful fetch (one `for-each-ref`).

Minor, after merge: it needs a default switch and a capped fetch at once.

add.issue.name: Requirement: no git operation may leave a state that blocks later work

edit.description.md:
From the user, 2026-10-13: a fetch, pull, push, clone or any other git operation epiq runs must never end in a state that blocks future work. "This must never ever happen."

What that means in practice:
- After any interruption — SIGKILL, SIGTERM, a timeout, a power loss, a laptop sleep — the next sync or fetch recovers on its own, without manual git commands.
- Nothing a crash leaves behind (a lock, a half-done rebase or cherry-pick, a stale ref lock, a truncated file) is allowed to make every later attempt fail or be skipped.
- User git config (signing, hooks) must not be able to wedge epiq's own bookkeeping.
- A linked repo's clone is a cache. Once it is broken locally, it is started over, never left failing.
- A wait past about 60 seconds counts as blocking.

Found by fault injection on main 903a8ade; tickets linked in comments.

add.issue.name: Board sync: a leftover CHERRY_PICK_HEAD wedges every later sync

edit.description.md:
Fault injection on main 903a8ade; also on 1.12.4. Reproduced through `syncEpiqWithRemote`.

Repro: leave an empty `packed-refs.lock` in the common git dir, as a killed `gc` or `pack-refs` does, then sync a divergent state branch. The rebase fails at its ref update, `rebaseWithRetry` retries and succeeds, the sync reports ok and pushes, and `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` stays with no `rebase-merge`. Every later sync then fails with `fatal: cannot do a partial commit during a cherry-pick`, even after the lock is gone; new events are never published.

Cause: `getInProgressGitOperation` (`git-utils.ts:722`) checks only `MERGE_HEAD` and the rebase dirs; `ensureSyncReady` (`sync.ts:119-168`) has no cherry-pick recovery.

Fix: detect `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `REVERT_HEAD` and `sequencer/`; with a `clean` or `dead` claim run `git cherry-pick --quit` (keeps the work tree); after any rebase, assert none remain. Regression test from the repro.

add.issue.name: Board sync: a stale lock on the remote-tracking state ref blocks every fetch

edit.description.md:
Fault injection on main 903a8ade; also on 1.12.4. Reproduced.

Repro: create `refs/remotes/origin/epiq/state.lock` (a fetch killed at its ref update leaves it, and so does the user's own `git fetch` killed in their checkout, whose default refspec covers `origin/epiq/state`). Every sync then fails with `cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/epiq/state'`.

Cause: `clearStaleRefLock` (`git-utils.ts:1046`) clears only `refs/heads/<branch>.lock`.

Fix: also clear `refs/remotes/origin/<stateBranch>.lock`. The user's own git can hold that one, so clear it only past an age of about 60s. Regression test from the repro.

add.issue.name: Board sync: the user's commit signing or a pre-rebase hook blocks every sync

edit.description.md:
Fault injection on main 903a8ade; also on 1.12.4. Both reproduced.

1. `commit.gpgsign=true` with a signer that fails: every sync fails with `gpg failed to sign the data`, and events stay staged but are never published. Realistic: a pinentry or 1Password prompt cannot answer during a background autosync. `git.commit` (`git-commands.ts:44-55`) and `rebaseOnto` (:78-82) do not pin signing.
2. A `pre-rebase` hook (via `core.hooksPath` or repo hooks) that exits 1: every sync fails with `The pre-rebase hook refused to rebase`; three rounds left three commits unpushed. `rebaseOnto` is the only state-branch write without `--no-verify`.

Fix: on every state-branch git call, `-c commit.gpgsign=false` and `-c core.hooksPath=<empty dir epiq owns>`, which also covers `reference-transaction` and `post-checkout`, as clone git already does. Regression tests for both.

add.issue.name: Board sync: a dead lock under a changed hostname skips syncs for 10 minutes; a stale claim still aborts a live rebase

edit.description.md:
Fault injection on main 903a8ade; also on 1.12.4.

1. A dead process's sync lock written under another hostname is only taken past `STALE_AFTER_MS`, 10 minutes (`sync-lock.ts:47`, :124). Every sync until then returns ok with `skipped: true`, so nothing says why. It takes a crash followed by a hostname change; on macOS `os.hostname()` follows the network, and the global dir is local. Fix: name the holder by a stable machine id kept in the global dir, not the hostname.
2. After a live holder's aged lock is broken as `stale`, `pullBranchRebaseIfPresent` (`git-utils.ts:1139`) still calls `abortRebaseIfPresent` unconditionally, which the claim rule forbids. In the stale-live runs it showed as "Failed to abort the rebase in progress" and a lost fetch-ref race on the second process; the board recovered. Fix: pass the claim down and skip the abort under `stale`.

Nit: the founder's clone fails `git fsck` with `missing tree 4b825dc6…` from the first sync, because `createStateBranch` (`git.ts:150`) runs `commit-tree` over the hardcoded empty tree without writing it. Harmless to sync. Run `git hash-object -w -t tree /dev/null` first.

add.issue.name: Linked repos: a crash or shutdown during a default-branch follow leaves the clone on the wrong branch for good

edit.description.md:
Fault injection on main (storm on 903a8ade; the code is unchanged on 8f6a53ae). Part of 7GC0E2M. 5F2GJKN's fix covers the cap's undo; this is the same wedge reached by an interruption, which runs no undo.

`fetchRepo` decides to follow by comparing the remote default with HEAD alone, and drops the other branches only on a fetch that just followed. `followDefaultBranch` writes HEAD and then the refspec in two separate git calls. So:
1. An interruption after the follow and before `dropOtherBranches` leaves the old default's ref. The next fetch finds HEAD already matching, so it neither follows nor drops, and under `branches: default` both branches are read for good.
2. An interruption between the two git calls leaves HEAD on the new default and the refspec on the old one. Every later fetch skips the follow and goes on fetching only the old branch: the clone silently stops tracking the repo's default.

Storm, upstream default switched mid-run: SIGKILL of node, 10 failures in 30; SIGTERM (clean shutdown), 20 in 30. Every other scenario was clean in all modes.

Fix: make the default-branch state an invariant checked on every fetch, not an event:
- under `default`, the refspec must name the remote's default;
- HEAD must point at it;
- every other head is dropped.
Decide from the refspec and the refs, never from HEAD alone. Regression test: kill between the two calls, and after the follow, then assert one head, the right refspec, and old-default-only commits gone.

add.issue.name: Linked repos: a clone broken locally is never started over (lost config, a redundant pack past the cap)

edit.description.md:
Part of 7GC0E2M. Reproduced through the real fetch on main b98f79c3, one deterministic corruption at a time, each followed by two fresh fetches.

Self-heals: an emptied `shallow`, every pack lost, refs and packed-refs emptied.

Wedges for good:
1. **Config emptied.** Every fetch fails with `'origin' does not appear to be a git repository`. `originOf` returns `unknown` for an unreadable origin and the clone is kept on purpose, so nothing ever starts it over.
2. **A redundant pack.** It is what a repack cut off between writing its new pack and deleting the old ones leaves. A clone holding 1.3 MB of history under a 2 MB cap reads as 2.7 MB on disk, and the "already past the cap" check refuses every fetch. Its message says to narrow the history, which would not help.

The clone is a cache. Fix, one rule that also covers corruptions nobody has listed yet:
- If the remote is reachable but the fetch fails, or the clone reads past the cap, delete the clone and clone it fresh under the lock, once.
- Report only a fresh clone's failure as the repo's own.
- The reachability test is cheap: every default-branch fetch already runs `ls-remote`.
- Guard against a loop: one re-clone per repo per some hours, recorded in the status file.

add.issue.name: Locks: a crashed holder's pid, reused by any live process, blocks for hours (clone lock 2h, project-file and sync locks 10 min)

edit.description.md:
Part of 7GC0E2M. Reproduced on main b98f79c3 by planting a lock that names pid 1, which is always alive, as a crashed holder's pid looks after reuse.

- **Clone lock:** every fetch answers "Being fetched by another process" for the full `CLONE_LOCK_STALE_MS`, 2 hours.
- **Project-file lock:** refuses edits ("Another process is editing .epiq/project.json") for its 10-minute stale limit.
- **Board sync lock:** the same rule, predating linked repos.

Cause: `claimOver` (`sync-lock.ts:130-132`) takes any live pid for the holder. Pid reuse is ordinary on a long-running machine.

Fix: record the holder's process start time in the lock and compare it with the pid's actual start time (`ps -o lstart= -p <pid>`, or /proc on Linux). At minimum, treat a lock whose `startedAt` is older than the system boot (`Date.now() - os.uptime()*1000`) as dead.

Same root, smaller: `writeStatus` (`commit-repo-fetch.ts:97`) names its temp file `.json.<pid>.tmp` with `wx`. A leftover under a reused live pid is never swept, and that process can never write the status, so the panel's fetch state goes stale. Use a random suffix. Also, the lock writer's `<lock>.<pid>.pending.lock` temp is never swept; not blocking.

add.issue.name: Linked repos: a clone that breaks again within 6 hours of a re-clone stays blocked until the 6 hours are up

edit.description.md:
Part of 7GC0E2M. Re-review of main at 5a1e26b4; reproduced through the real fetch.

Repro: empty a clone's config and fetch. It is re-cloned and works. Empty it again: every fetch fails with `'origin' does not appear to be a git repository` until 6 hours after the first re-clone. Over 60 seconds counts as blocking.

Cause: `mayStartOver` applies the 6-hour `RESTART_INTERVAL_MS` to the unambiguous local case, a clone failing `cloneOpens`, as well as to the remote-attributed `brokeHere` case. And `restartedAt` is written whenever a re-clone was attempted, not when one landed. A re-clone that failed against a broken remote therefore also blocks a genuine local break for the next 6 hours.

Fix:
- Gate only the `brokeHere` path by the interval. A clone failing `cloneOpens` is always re-cloned, or backs off 1, then 10, then 60 minutes.
- Record `restartedAt` only for a re-clone that landed.

Cost, related: `brokeHere` (`commit-repo-fetch.ts:973`) reads "ls-remote answers, fetch failed" as local breakage. One connection reset mid-pack therefore re-downloads the whole repo. Retry the fetch once first, or re-clone only on a `cloneOpens` failure or a local cause in git's error. A healthy clone is never deleted: the old one stays until the new one lands.

add.issue.name: Linked repos: re-clone attempts that never reached the remote, or were cut by shutdown, climb the backoff to an hour

edit.description.md:
Part of 7GC0E2M. Fault injection on main at 6e2a5282; both reproduced.

**1. A shutdown during a re-clone counts as a failed attempt.** 17 of 20 runs failed.
- Repro: empty a clone's config so the fetch takes the re-clone path, throttle the transfer, then SIGTERM the process.
- Result: the next fetches fail with `'origin' does not appear to be a git repository`, with `restarts=1`, for 1 minute. A second interruption costs 10 minutes and a third 60.
- Closing the TUI or MCP server mid-re-clone is enough.
- Cause: the SIGTERM handler gives clone git 2s to exit (`git-utils.ts:295`). The killed re-clone returns failed, and the status write counts it (`commit-repo-fetch.ts:1178-1182`).

**2. Attempts against an unreachable remote climb the backoff.**
- Repro: a clone that won't open while the remote is gone. Three passes raise `restarts` to 3. After the remote returns, every fetch fails until 60 minutes after the last try.
- Realistic case: a laptop offline through about 11 minutes of autosync, with a clone that broke locally.
- Cause: line 1131 re-clones whenever `backedOff` allows, and every failed attempt is counted, including ones that never reached the remote.

Fix for both: count an attempt only when the re-clone reached the remote and failed there.
- Skip stamping `restartTriedAt` and bumping `restarts` when the process is shutting down (a flag set in the signal handler).
- Before re-cloning a clone that won't open, run `ls-remote`. If the remote does not answer, skip without counting.

**Cost, after merge.** When the remote answers `ls-remote` but every fetch fails, failed re-clones never set `restartedAt`. The 6-hour window (`mayStartOverFailedFetch`, :985-989) therefore never starts, and re-clones repeat hourly, each up to a full download. Count that window from `restartTriedAt` on the "remote answers" path.

Everything else held on 6e2a5282:
- Kill storm: 0 failures on the default switch and on fetch, under SIGKILL and SIGTERM, and 0 on re-clone under SIGKILL.
- One dropped fetch is retried with no re-clone.
- Remote down: the clone is kept.
- Every crash point recovers on the first fetch.
- Backoff resets after a clean fetch.

add.issue.comment.md:
Plan review (claude/reviewer). The base is sound. The events are append-only, one file per actor, so they cannot conflict. Causal order (a forest by refId, siblings by id) gives every replica holding the same set the same fold. The live-log fold, rather than the singleton, is right because of time travel.

Changes I'd ask for:
1. Keep version-sensitive rules out of the fold. A skip rule in a handler becomes permanent format, and two client versions with different rules disagree on the list.
   - Cap: fold every connect, and have readers take the first 20 live in causal order. Do not skip at 20, which freezes MAX_REPOS forever.
   - Labels (c): keep them in state, and resolve a collision at display time: the earliest in causal order keeps the label, the rest show their basename. Dropping the label in the handler means it never comes back once the holder disconnects.
   - isAllowedRepoUrl: keep it in the fold for security, and also re-check it at fetch with the current rules. Only ever tighten it.
2. (a) Treat connect on a live repo as an upsert: merge its fields under edit's last-writer-wins. A skip silently drops the later writer's options when two people connect the same repo at once. The write side already turns it into an edit, so the fold should agree.
3. Write side: the cap and label checks are advisory, because a pull can insert an earlier sibling and change the fold after the fact. Say so in the reply ("connected; N repos are over the limit"), and let the GUI show a connect that falls past the cap rather than having it vanish.
4. (d) Do the sweep in this ticket, keyed only on a positive tombstone: a disconnected entry in a fold that read successfully. Write the existing removal mark, and let today's sweep delete. Never act on absence. A [] read must not move anything.
5. Disconnect order: persist the event first, then delete the local clone.
6. Probe:
   - use `ls-remote -- <url>` through forClone (no prompt, protocol allow-list, neutral cwd);
   - a reconnect of a disconnected repo counts as new and is probed;
   - say in the reply that ssh-agent or a credential helper must already work, since a passphrase prompt cannot be answered.
7. Repo id pin: cover several URL shapes (trailing .git, a trailing slash, host case, scp form against ssh://) so that a change to normalization fails a test, not users.
8. Exhaustive per-action maps (format-log-utils, scrubber series, the TUI log) need entries for the three new actions, or the log panel shows raw actions.

(e) Do not restrict disconnect. Reconnecting is cheap, and anyone can already move or close tickets. unlink.contributor.email is restricted because it is about identity.

(f) A trust-model change for jola (parked, not blocking). With project.json, connecting a repo for everyone took a commit that could be reviewed. As an event, any board participant or agent makes every teammate's machine clone that URL on the next sync: up to 20 × 2 GB, and fetches under their credentials to a host of the writer's choosing. A file:/// URL clones a local path on each teammate's machine. That may be acceptable, but it should be a conscious decision. One option is an aggregate disk cap per board.

Review of PR #462 (9397eea9), part 1 of 2, from claude/reviewer.

Green: the gate (unit 2381, GUI 233), TUI e2e 40/40, collab 17/17.

Fault injection:
- Kill storm: 84 runs (random SIGKILL/SIGTERM/group kills, plus fixed crash points: after the confirm event and before the rename, during the disconnect delete, mid stage-clone). Every next pass recovers with no leftovers and a clean fsck.
- Confirm racing a fetch: the stage is adopted every time, never cloned twice.
- Disconnect then reconnect, within one process and across two: ends live and cloned.
- v1.12.4: syncs, writes and boots a board holding the new events plus 21 hostile lines. The lines stay byte-identical, and the new build derives the same list on both clones.
- Hostile payloads (`--upload-pack`, `ext::`, `-oProxyCommand`, `../../../etc`, `__proto__`, null/array/100 KB): all harmless, and nothing was touched outside `repos/<projectId>/`.

BLOCKER
1. A failed persist leaves a phantom on this machine, in both directions. The handler changes `state.repos` in place before the persist. When the persist fails (ENOSPC is realistic right after a 2 GB stage), the next successful write's `noteOwnAppend` makes `accountedSignature` match again. `liveRegistry` then serves the state, which no log holds.
   - Connect: the confirm hits ENOSPC, a ticket is created, and the fetch then lists and clones a repo that is in no log.
   - Disconnect: the persist hits ENOSPC, a ticket is created, and the fetch then has `sweepDisconnected` delete the clone of a repo the log says is live.
   - Repro: zz-probe1.test.ts in the reviewer's scratch.
   - Fix: apply to a copy and commit it only after the persist succeeds, or invalidate the shortcut on any failed write (mark the state stale until a reload). Add a regression test for each direction.

HIGH
2. Version-sensitive rules still sit in the fold, against the file's own header.
   - `MAX_URL_LENGTH` (2048) and `isAllowedRepoUrl` both skip a connect in `applyRepoEvent`. Change either in a later build and two builds disagree on which ids exist, and then which edits and disconnects land.
   - `resolveRepos` re-checks the URL anyway. Let the fold accept any string url (bounded only by the line size) and filter in readers only, so the registry is identical across all versions.
3. `repoIdOf` lowercases the whole URL, and that id is permanent format. `…/Team/Repo` and `…/team/repo` (and `file:///srv/Repo` against `file:///srv/repo`) give one id, so the second merges into the first. That is wrong on case-sensitive hosts and file systems.
   - Lowercase only the scheme and the host; keep the path as typed.
   - Decide now. After release it can never change.

add.issue.comment.md:
Review of PR #462, part 2 of 2.

MEDIUM
4. TUI terminal injection. `describeRepoPreview` prints the latest commit's subject and author raw, and those come from the repo being previewed, which may be hostile. Run both through `sanitizeInlineText`, as commit-timeline does.
5. Labels can show duplicates. `resolveRepos` only counts explicitly wanted labels as taken, never basenames.
   - Repro: connect `file:///…/up` (no label, shows "up"), then `https://x.invalid/a/up` with label "up". Both show "up", and "could not fetch up" names neither.
   - It works the other way round too: a later repo can squat an earlier one's basename, and the earlier one can't claim it (label == basename → "Unchanged").
   - Fix: count basenames in the resolution, and fall back to the id when the basename is taken. Disconnect by an ambiguous name is already refused, which is good.
6. Stage disk use is unbounded: one stage of up to 2 GB per repo, for 15 minutes, with no limit on the total. An agent previewing 20 repos holds about 40 GB. Allow one stage per process: a new preview of another repo drops the old one, or is refused.

LOW
7. `sweepPending` judges a stage's owner by pid alone. A dead process's stage under a reused pid stays until that pid dies. Use the start-time check the locks already have.
8. The sweep on another machine leaves an empty `<id>.git.removed` that is never cleared, unless the repo is reconnected. Remove it after the delete succeeds.
9. A disconnect when there are more than 20 repos starts the 21st fetching on every machine, with no new confirm. It's defensible, since the confirm said "past the limit", but it should be deliberate: say so in the over-limit confirm text.

FINE
- The payloads are intent only.
- edit.repo is justified.
- The fold defaults are pinned.
- First spelling wins, and a revive takes its own.

Seen outside this PR, not verified: after a sync, a `~pending-…jsonl` still held an `add.issue` line already folded into the tracked log. This PR doesn't touch sync, so it's for a separate look at pending-log dedup.

Verdict: request changes. #1 blocks. #2 and #3 are format decisions that get much more expensive after release.
